title: Installation & Setup
description: Run Lupis Engine directly in your web browser, download the standalone desktop executable from GitHub, launch with Docker, or host the local servers yourself.

blocks.content: You can use **Lupis Engine** in four ways depending on your workflow. Choose the browser version for instant access, the desktop executable for offline creation, or Docker and local servers when you need backend font generation and desktop **.EXE** packaging.

items.title: Web Studio
items.desc: Open the editor directly in a WebGL 2.0 browser with zero installation.

items.title: Desktop Executable
items.desc: Download the prebuilt release from GitHub for offline desktop game development.

items.title: Docker Compose
items.desc: Start the editor, runtime, and backend export service together with one command.

items.title: Self-Hosted Server
items.desc: Run the Node.js editor and backend services directly on your machine.

rows: Quick prototyping and learning without installing software.
Chrome, Edge, or Firefox with WebGL 2.0 enabled.
Offline desktop workflow with no command-line setup.
Full local environment including custom font conversion and **.EXE** export.
Local hosting and custom server configuration without Docker.

blocks.content: The fastest way to start is through the hosted [Lupis Engine Web Studio](https://lupis-engine.web.app). Your projects and assets are stored locally inside your browser using the Origin Private File System (OPFS).

items: Open the **Lupis Engine Web Studio** link above in a modern browser such as Google Chrome, Microsoft Edge, or Mozilla Firefox.
On the **My Projects** dashboard, click **New** to create a fresh project or drag and drop an existing **.lupisproject** file onto the page.
Click your project card to launch the [Editor Overview](interface/editor_overview) workspace and start building.

blocks.message: Browser storage is tied to your current browser profile. Export a **.lupisproject** archive regularly (see [Project & Export](getting_started/project_and_export)) to back up your work or move it to another device.

blocks.content: If you prefer a dedicated desktop application that works offline, download the official prebuilt executable from [Lupis Engine GitHub Releases](https://github.com/haikal-adnan/lupis-engine/releases).

items: Open the **GitHub Releases** page linked above in your browser.
Under the latest release **Assets** section, download the desktop executable or archive for your operating system.
Extract the archive (if zipped) to a folder on your computer and launch the **Lupis Engine** executable.
When the **My Projects** dashboard appears, click **New** to create your first offline project.

blocks.content: Running with [Docker](https://www.docker.com/) launches the visual editor, the standalone core runtime, and the backend packaging service in one step. Clone the [Lupis Engine GitHub Repository](https://github.com/haikal-adnan/lupis-engine) and run the following commands in your terminal:

blocks.snippet:
git clone https://github.com/haikal-adnan/lupis-engine.git
cd lupis-engine
docker compose -f start.yml up

blocks.content: Once the containers finish starting, open the editor in your browser using the ports below:

rows: Main dashboard, scene editor, and visual scripting studio.
Processes custom font atlases and compiles Windows **.EXE** builds.

blocks.content: You can also run the services directly on your computer using [Node.js](https://nodejs.org/) (version **20.19+** or **22.12+**) without Docker.

items: Clone the [Lupis Engine GitHub Repository](https://github.com/haikal-adnan/lupis-engine) to your computer.
Open a terminal in the **service** folder, install dependencies, and start the backend server on port **37602**.
Open a second terminal in the **editor** folder, install dependencies, and start the visual editor on port **37600**.
Optionally, open a third terminal in the **core** folder and serve the standalone runtime on port **37601**.
Navigate to **http://localhost:37600** in your browser to open the studio.

blocks.snippet:
# Terminal 1: Backend service (http://localhost:37602)
cd service && npm install && npm run dev

# Terminal 2: Visual editor (http://localhost:37600)
cd editor && npm install && npm run dev

# Terminal 3: Standalone core runtime (optional, http://localhost:37601)
cd core && npx serve -l 37601 .

blocks.message: Keep the backend **service** terminal running on port **37602** whenever you import custom **.ttf** or **.otf** fonts or build a Windows **.EXE** package.
